Worked out solution

Step 1: The first step here is to pick \(u\) and \(dv\) such that \( \displaystyle \int udv = u \cdot v - \int vdu\).


Step 2: For this problem well use the following choices for \(u\) and \(dv\)

\(u = {@func_var_u@}\), \(dv ={@func_var_dv@} dx\),
Next, we need to compute \(du\) (by differentiating \(u\)) and \(v\) (by integrating \(\frac{du}{dx}\)).

\(\frac{du}{dx}= {@diff_u@}\), \(v= {@int_v@}\)

Step 3: Plugging the above back into the Integration by Parts formula \( \displaystyle \int udv = u \cdot v - \int vdu\):

\( \displaystyle \int ({@func_var_u@}){@func_var_dv@} dx = ({@int_v@})({@func_var_u@}) - \displaystyle \int ({@int_v@})({@diff_u@}) dx\)


Step 4: To evaluate the integral \(\displaystyle \int {@v_du@} dx\), we will need to apply integration by parts using the formula \( \displaystyle \int s\cdot dt = s \cdot t - \int t\cdot ds\).

\(s={@diff_u@}\) and \(dt={@int_v@}dx\)


\(ds={@diff(diff_u)@}\) and \(t={@int(int_v,x)@} \)


Now

\(\begin{align} \displaystyle \int ({@int_v@})({@diff_u@}) dx & =({@diff_u@})({@int(int_v,x)@})-\displaystyle \int({@int(int_v,x)@}) ({@diff(diff_u)/del(x)@})dx \\ & = ({@diff_u*int(int_v,x)@})-\displaystyle \int{@int(int_v,x)*diff(diff_u)/del(x)@}dx \end{align}\)


\(\begin{align} \displaystyle \int ({@func_var_u@}){@func_var_dv@} dx & = ({@int_v@})({@func_var_u@}) - ({@diff_u*int(int_v,x)@})+\displaystyle \int{@int(int_v,x)*diff(diff_u)/del(x)@}dx \\ \displaystyle \int ({@func_var_u@}){@func_var_dv@} dx - \displaystyle \int {@int(int_v,x)*diff(diff_u)/del(x)@}dx &= ({@int_v@})({@func_var_u@}) - {@diff_u*int(int_v,x)@})\\ \int {@func_var_u*func_var_dv - int(int_v,x)*diff(diff_u)/del(x)@}\, dx & = ({@int_v@})({@func_var_u@}) - {@diff_u*int(int_v,x)@}\\ \displaystyle \int ({@func_var_u@}){@func_var_dv@} dx & ={@ta@} \end{align}\)
